From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs — next steps

Ben — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. TL;DR: main pain is unpredictable tail latency causing poor user experience during peaks; goal is consistent 95th %-ile latency under 250ms for chat-like flows and ability to sustain ~50 concurrent low-latency sessions (avg token length ~512).

What we heard (pain & goals):
- Current system sees 95th %-ile spikes up to ~1.2s during bursts — affects product metrics and conversion.
- Need predictable latency (95p < 250ms) and steady throughput for daytime peak.
- Data residency: must run in VPC with audit logs retained 1 year.
- Model requirements: you want an open-weight model (Llama-2 / similar) and ability to switch to larger models during complex workflows.

Sizing & SLO notes (from call):
- Target SLOs: 95p latency <= 250ms for <512 token requests; p50 ~60ms.
- Concurrent steady-state target: 50 concurrent interactive sessions; burst to 150 for short windows.
- Typical prompt+response token budget: 400–700 tokens; long-run cache hit expected for repeated prefixes.

Recommended Redwood approach (what we propose):
1) Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) in your VPC to guarantee capacity and isolation.
2) KV/prefix caching for common prompts to reduce compute and tail-latency exposure.
3) Batch tuning + dynamic batching window to balance throughput vs latency; we’ll target sub-250ms 95p in canary.
4) Quantization profile and model variant plan (13B/30B fallbacks) so we can trade cost/latency during bursts.

Attachments: SLO-matrix (breakdown of targets & test scenarios), deployment topology diagram, draft mutual action plan.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood: produce a short TPS/latency test plan and deployment topology (Logan will own the tech write-up) — ETA 48 hours.
- Acme: share a sampled production traces export (or synthetic scenarios) and the compliance contact for VPC/KMS integration.
- Schedule a canary run planning call next week to align on rollback/fallback (I’ll send a Doodle).

If that matches your notes, I’ll get the test plan and topology over by Wednesday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

Ben / Marissa — adding a few technical clarifications and the proposed deployment topology summary so the Acme infra team gets visibility. I’ve included the rough rollout and test plan in the attachment.

Key infra notes:
- Deployment topology: Dedicated GPU pool in your VPC (c4/g5 equivalent) fronted by a lightweight stateless router. We’ll run 2 AZ-distributed replicas for failover; autoscale based on queue length with fast warm pools for burst handling. See redwood-deploy-topology.png.
- Caching: deploy a shared Redis-backed prefix cache for common prompts + in-memory KV caching on the model nodes for hot sessions. Cache TTLs tuned to 1–6 hours depending on workload. Cache-hit reduces tail-latency dramatically.
- Batching strategy: dynamic batching with short 2–6ms queue windows during steady-state; aggressive smaller windows during interactive sessions to hit p50/p95 targets.
- Quantization & model variants: recommend starting with 13B int8 quantized for steady-state; enable 30B fp16 fallback for heavy/complex queries with an automated routing policy (route by latency budget + query complexity). We’ll expose a routing rule set so product can mark sessions as high-priority.
- Observability: token-level latency/cost metrics, per-model dashboards, and a synthetic canary (1000 requests across the expected token distributions) to validate 95p SLA.

Test plan items we’ll deliver in the doc:
1) Synthetic trace runner + harness config (workload shapes)
2) Canary gating thresholds and rollback triggers
3) Cost/throughput sensitivity matrix (attached SLO-matrix).

Logistics:
- I’ll push the topology PNG and an initial test-run checklist to the Drive link Marissa shared.
- For KMS/VPC integration we’ll need your security contact to exchange a short network runbook and temporary test credentials (no keys stored).

If you want, we can run a quick 30-min ops walkthrough before the canary.

— Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
